es.summary: Agonista dopaminérgico de acción corta usado por vía subcutánea como medicamento de rescate para episodios "off" en la enfermedad de Parkinson avanzada.
key_points: Se administra solo por vía subcutánea.
Indicado para episodios agudos de inmovilidad ("off") en Parkinson avanzado.
Puede producir hipotensión severa, náuseas y vómitos.
Contraindicado con antieméticos antagonistas 5‑HT3 (p. ej., ondansetrón).
No tiene antídoto específico; el manejo es de soporte.

mechanism: Estimula directamente los receptores dopaminérgicos D1 y D2 en el sistema nervioso central.
Aumenta la actividad dopaminérgica, mejorando la transmisión motora.
Acción de corta duración permite uso intermitente para episodios "off".
indications: Tratamiento agudo e intermitente de episodios de hipomovilidad en Parkinson avanzado.
Uso como rescate cuando la medicación oral no controla los síntomas "off".
contraindications: Hipersensibilidad a la apomorfina o a sus excipientes.
Uso concomitante de antagonistas 5‑HT3 (ondansetrón, granisetrón, etc.).
adverse_effects: Hipotensión severa con pérdida de consciencia (grave).
Reacciones en el sitio de inyección: erytema, dolor (común).
interactions: Antieméticos 5‑HT3 aumentan riesgo de hipotensión profunda.
Antihipertensivos pueden potenciar la caída de presión arterial.
Otros agonistas dopaminérgicos pueden intensificar efectos dopaminérgicos.
Inhibidores de MAO pueden aumentar efectos adversos dopaminérgicos.
nursing_care: Evaluar presión arterial y frecuencia cardíaca antes de cada dosis; retener si PA sistólica <90 mmHg.
Observar signos de hipotensión ortostática (mareos, visión borrosa).
Monitorear náuseas, vómitos y estado del sitio de inyección.
Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si ocurre hipotensión severa o pérdida de consciencia.
Rotar los sitios de inyección subcutánea para evitar irritación.
patient_teaching: Administrar la inyección subcutánea en abdomen, muslo o brazo, rotando los sitios.
Evitar tomar antieméticos 5‑HT3 sin consultar al profesional de salud.
Reconocer síntomas de hipotensión (mareos, visión tenue) y buscar ayuda inmediata.
Mantener registro de los episodios "off" y de la respuesta al medicamento.
No compartir la solución; desechar el dispositivo según indicaciones.

en.summary: Short‑acting dopaminergic agonist administered subcutaneously as a rescue medication for "off" episodes in advanced Parkinson disease.
key_points: Indicated for acute immobility episodes ("off") in advanced Parkinson disease.
May cause severe hypotension, nausea, and vomiting.
No specific antidote; management is supportive.

mechanism: Directly stimulates central nervous system D1 and D2 dopamine receptors.
Increases dopaminergic activity, improving motor transmission.
Short duration of action allows intermittent use for "off" episodes.
indications: Acute, intermittent treatment of hypomobility episodes in advanced Parkinson disease.
Rescue use when oral medication fails to control "off" symptoms.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to apomorphine or its excipients.
Concurrent use of 5‑HT3 antagonists (ondansetron, granisetron, etc.).
Intravenous administration; only subcutaneous use is permitted.
adverse_effects: Severe hypotension with loss of consciousness (serious).
interactions: 5‑HT3 antiemetics increase risk of profound hypotension.
Antihypertensives may potentiate blood pressure drop.
Other dopaminergic agonists can intensify dopaminergic effects.
MAO inhibitors may increase dopaminergic adverse effects.
nursing_care: Assess blood pressure and heart rate before each dose; hold if systolic BP <90 mmHg.
Observe for orthostatic hypotension signs (dizziness, blurred vision).
Monitor nausea, vomiting, and injection site status.
Hold dose and notify provider if severe hypotension or loss of consciousness occurs.
Rotate subcutaneous injection sites to prevent irritation.
patient_teaching: Administer subcutaneous injection in abdomen, thigh, or arm, rotating sites.
Avoid taking 5‑HT3 antiemetics without consulting a health professional.
Recognize hypotension symptoms (dizziness, blurred vision) and seek immediate help.
Keep a record of "off" episodes and response to medication.
Do not share the solution; discard the device as instructed.

summary.0.quote: Apomorphine hydrocloride injection is a non-ergoline dopamine agonist indicated for the acute, intermittent treatment of hypomobility, "off" episodes ("end-of-dose wearing off" and unpredictable "on/off" episodes) associated with advanced Parkinson's disease ( 1 ) 2 DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION For subcutaneous use only ( 2.1 ) Alway

key_points.3.quote: Based on reports of profound hypotension and loss of consciousness when apomorphine was administered with ondansetron, the concomitant use of apomorphine with drugs of the 5HT 3 antagonist class including antiemetics (for example, ondansetron, granisetron, dolasetron, palonosetron) and alosetron are contraindicated [see Contraindications (4) ].

sections.mechanism.1.quote: Dopaminergic substances increase dopamine-related activity in the brain.

sections.indications.0.quote: Apomorphine hydrocloride injection is a non-ergoline dopamine agonist indicated for the acute, intermittent treatment of hypomobility, "off" episodes ("end-of-dose wearing off" and unpredictable "on/off" episodes) associated with advanced Parkinson's disease ( 1 )

sections.indications.1.quote: This drug is reserved as an acute “rescue” medication to treat “off” episodes in between doses or “off-on” periods that occur randomly in clients with advanced PD.

sections.contraindications.0.quote: Hypersensitivity to apomorphine, its excipients or sodium metabisulfite ( 4 , 5.12 )

sections.contraindications.1.quote: Based on reports of profound hypotension and loss of consciousness when apomorphine was administered with ondansetron, the concomitant use of apomorphine with drugs of the 5HT 3 antagonist class including antiemetics (for example, ondansetron, granisetron, dolasetron, palonosetron) and alosetron are contraindicated [see Contraindications (4) ].

sections.contraindications.2.quote: For subcutaneous use only; thrombus formation and pulmonary embolism have followed intravenous administration of apomorphine hydrocloride ( 5.1 )

sections.adverse_effects.0.quote: The most common adverse reactions (apomorphine hydrocloride incidence at least 10% greater than placebo incidence) observed in a placebo-controlled trial were yawning, drowsiness/somnolence, dyskinesias, dizziness/postural hypotension, rhinorrhea, nausea and/or vomiting, hallucination/confusion, and edema/swelling of extremities.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: The most common adverse reactions specific to this drug are excessive yawning, injection-site reactions, rhinorrhea, and cardiac issues.
